intent.raw: Full refine of mutation execution mechanics: how ApplyApprovedBatch turns approved MutationTasks into the next revision HTML. Get the model and architecture right; it could be a mix of mutation task with deterministic validators; evaluate each approach.
intent.objective: Choose and design the mutation-execution model + architecture (deterministic-patch vs agentic-regeneration vs hybrid agentic-propose + deterministic-validate), with a toy-game falsification and a non-executed implementation plan.
intent.operator_sentence: We need to get the model and architecture right; it could be a mix of mutation task with deterministic validators; evaluate each approach.

technique_overlays.trigger: Ordinary refinement requires ordered stage handoff, validation, owner boundaries, and observability.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Each non-first stage consumes a prior frame/handle/decision and records a receipt; owner boundaries preserved.

technique_overlays.trigger: Three plausible execution models (deterministic-patch, agentic-regeneration, hybrid-validated) must be compared, not assumed.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Each approach gets an advocate; elimination/convergence criteria and rejected alternatives are recorded; selection is a non-dominated pareto choice across auditability, expressiveness, runtime fit, and ergonomics.

technique_overlays.trigger: Determinism/auditability and agentic flexibility are competing principles that must be preserved until synthesis.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Determinism-guardian and flexibility-advocate roles are preserved; each contested point becomes a decision, a residue, or a deferred option; the design states where determinism lives.

technique_overlays.trigger: The selected execution model must survive a controlled apply before planning.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: A sample MutationTask is applied to sample HTML under the chosen model; expected evidence and failure interpretation are named; repair feeds the plan.

subagent_strategy.trigger: Evaluating three competing execution models fairly needs independent advocates plus a deterministic-validator designer and a toy-game runner; one voice would bias the tournament.
subagent_strategy.explanation: The tournament and dialectic depend on independent perspectives: an advocate per approach argues its strongest case, a validator-designer specifies the deterministic checks, and a toy-game runner falsifies the chosen model. Parent synthesis joins their receipts. Role-bound sibling agents with isolated framing produce a fairer comparison than a single chain.
context: Apply currently does no HTML mutation; the model is undesigned, so a fair multi-approach evaluation is high-value.
Operator asked for a full refine to get the model and architecture right and to evaluate each approach.
Operator has approved subagent spend across this project's design sessions.

roles.purpose: Argue the strongest case for Approach A (deterministic typed-patch transformer).
Argue the strongest case for Approach B (Claude Code regenerates the HTML).
Argue the strongest case for Approach C (agentic-propose + deterministic-validate).
Specify the deterministic validator set and where determinism must live, independent of which approach wins.
Falsify the chosen model by applying a sample MutationTask to sample HTML and interpreting failures.
Join advocate/validator/toy-game receipts into the chosen model + architecture.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run the full mutation-execution refine with 6 role-bound subagents (3 approach advocates + validator-designer + toy-game runner + synthesis), pareto join? Approve subagent execution under dispatch refine-ups-mutation-exec-20260615.

steps.name: Context Builder evidence baseline
stop_conditions: Baseline cites apply-approved-batch.ts, MutationTask/DiffSummary, synthesis determinism, the CLI-native runtime, and data-od-id.

steps.name: Invoke Define — the execution problem + candidate approaches
Distill — tournament of the three execution approaches
convergence_criteria: Each approach is scored on auditability/determinism, change expressiveness, Claude Code-native fit, data-od-id stability, and apply-gate ergonomics (OQ-2).
Dominated approaches are eliminated with recorded reasons; the non-dominated selection (or a synthesis) is named.
Rejected alternatives are preserved in a residue ledger.
stop_conditions: One model selected (likely the hybrid synthesis) with a pareto rationale; no further rounds once scores stop changing.

steps.name: Invoke Design — execution model + architecture (determinism vs flexibility dialectic)
convergence_criteria: States where determinism lives (synthesis, validators, or both) and why.
Specifies the MutationTask/DiffSummary schema changes, the apply state machine, and the deterministic validator set.
Each determinism-vs-flexibility tension becomes a decision, a residue, or a deferred option, with an ergonomics rationale.

steps.name: Distill Repair — toy-game falsification of the chosen model
stop_conditions: A sample MutationTask applied to sample HTML under the chosen model; failures interpreted; repairs recorded or design adjusted.

gates.condition: Each runtime-backed stage names its native capability handle and expected receipt before execution.
External research runs only if a named gap appears and the operator confirms; default local-first.
Tournament records advocate entries, elimination/convergence criteria, and rejected alternatives before a model is selected.
The chosen model is falsified on a sample apply with named expected evidence and failure interpretation before planning.
Stage capabilities own their native artifacts; refine does not rewrite them; no SPEC/operations/architecture mutation without operator approval (proposals only).
RESULT.md is synthesized from stage artifacts (not the route proposal) and names the chosen model, residue, and next routes.
Subagent execution is approved before any subagent spawns.

promotion_guardrails: Refine does not mutate SPEC.md, operations.md, architecture.md, or the ledger as canonical truth; it proposes, and changes are applied only on operator approval.
Stage capabilities own their native artifacts; the manifest references them.
External research stays external_context until owner review.
